concept: Mean of grouped data and modal class
prompt:
The times, $t$ minutes, that 60 students took to complete a task are shown.

| Time | $0<t\le10$ | $10<t\le20$ | $20<t\le30$ | $30<t\le40$ | $40<t\le50$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 6 | 14 | 22 | 12 | 6 |

**(a)** Write down the modal class. **[1]**

**(b)** Estimate the mean time. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $20<t\le30$ **(A1)**

**(b)** Use midpoints $5,15,25,35,45$: $\dfrac{30+210+550+420+270}{60}$ **(M1)** $\approx24.7$ min **(A1)**

It is an *estimate* because the exact times within each class are unknown.

prompt: Explain why the modal class of grouped data does not tell you the mode of the original data.
markscheme: The modal class is the class with the highest frequency; the individual values inside it are unknown, and the most common single value could even lie in a different class **(R1)**

prompt:
For the data $2,\ 3,\ 3,\ 5,\ 7,\ 8,\ 30$:

**(a)** find the mean, median and mode; **[2]**

**(b)** state which measure best represents a typical value, with a reason. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Mean $=\dfrac{58}{7}\approx8.29$, median $5$, mode $3$ **(A2)**

**(b)** The median: the outlier 30 pulls the mean above six of the seven values, while the median is unaffected **(R1)**

prompt: Find the standard deviation and variance of $4,\ 7,\ 7,\ 9,\ 13$.
markscheme:
Mean $8$; squared deviations $16,1,1,1,25$, sum $44$ **(M1)**

Variance $\dfrac{44}{5}=8.8$; standard deviation $\sqrt{8.8}\approx2.97$ **(A1)**

(IB uses the population standard deviation $\sigma$, dividing by $n$; this is what the GDC labels $\sigma_x$.)

prompt: A data set has mean 8 and standard deviation 2.97. Each value is doubled and then 5 is added. Find the new mean, standard deviation and variance.
markscheme:
Mean: $2(8)+5=21$ **(A1)**

Standard deviation: $2(2.97)=5.93$ — adding a constant shifts every value equally, so spread is unchanged by $+5$ **(A1)**

Variance: $2^{2}\times8.8=35.2$ **(A1)**

prompt: Find the median and the interquartile range of $3,\ 5,\ 6,\ 8,\ 9,\ 11,\ 12,\ 15$.
